q: Does the linear-in-p small-p scaling of the noisy-VQE energy shift survive when the noise model is generalized from independent local depolarizing to spatially/temporally correlated noise (crosstalk, 1/f dephasing) or coherent overrotation errors?
basis: The paper's Eq. (6) noise model assumes independent single-gate Kraus channels; our replication inherits this assumption. Real superconducting hardware exhibits ZZ crosstalk between neighboring qubits and coherent unitary errors from imperfect pulse calibration, both of which can violate the linear-accumulation ansatz. This gap was not addressed in the paper or our replication.
next_steps: In the existing harness, replace `add_all_qubit_quantum_error(depolarizing_error(p, k))` with (a) a `QuantumChannel` built from two-qubit correlated Pauli errors on nearest-neighbor pairs at strength p, and (b) coherent Rx/Rz overrotations at angle sqrt(p). Rerun the n=4 d=2/3 sweep and fit DeltaE(p) to p, p*log(p), and p^alpha. Report the deviation from linearity and whether the per-gate-slope intensiveness (C6) is preserved.

q: How much of the noise-induced energy shift can be recovered by modern error-mitigation methods (zero-noise extrapolation, probabilistic error cancellation, Clifford data regression) applied post-hoc to the noisy expectation values reported here?
basis: The paper predates the widespread adoption of ZNE/PEC (Kandala et al. 2019, Temme et al. 2017, Czarnik et al. 2021) and does not attempt any mitigation. Whether the observed linear DeltaE(p) can be canceled by Richardson extrapolation is a distinct empirical question with direct hardware relevance.
next_steps: Use the existing d=2 sweep at p in {1e-4, 3e-4, 1e-3, 3e-3, 1e-2}: fit E(p) to a low-order polynomial in p and extrapolate to p=0 via Richardson. Compare the extrapolated E(0) against our measured E(0)=-5.0466 and against E_0=-5.2263. Report residual error vs mitigation order. Then rerun with folded-CNOT ZNE at noise scales lambda in {1, 3, 5} at fixed p=1e-3 (mitiq-compatible).

q: Does the fixed-theta* protocol we used mask a noise-induced barren-plateau (NIBP) effect that would appear if VQE were re-optimized under noise?
basis: Wang et al. (Nat. Commun. 2021) showed that local Pauli noise flattens the VQE cost landscape exponentially in circuit depth; the paper we replicated does not address gradient variance and neither does our fixed-theta* protocol. Our observed linear DeltaE(p) is measured at a fixed optimal noiseless point, not at a re-optimized noisy minimum.
next_steps: Modify vqe_noisy.py to re-run COBYLA inside the noise loop (cost function = Tr(rho(theta) H) at each p). Compute (a) the variance Var[dE/dtheta_i] over 20 random theta samples at each p, and (b) the noisy re-optimized energy E_min(p). Test whether Var falls exponentially in d for d in {2, 3, 4, 5} at p=1e-3, matching the NIBP prediction Var ~ exp(-c*d).

q: Do device-specific composite noise models (e.g., IBM Falcon r5.11H depolarizing + T1/T2 + readout confusion matrix; Rigetti Aspen-M-3 crosstalk profile; Quantinuum H2 ion-trap fidelity model) yield the same qualitative monotonic + linear + depth-accumulation picture, or does hardware realism break the scaling?
basis: The paper's Sec. IV composite IBM model (their C9, which we did not test) is the only device-specific comparison. Newer NISQ devices (2024-2026 vintage) have T1/T2 imbalance and mid-circuit measurement noise that the depolarizing model does not capture. Whether the paper's scaling laws survive is an open, hardware-relevant question.
next_steps: Build three `NoiseModel` instances in Qiskit Aer using calibration data pulled from `IBMProvider().get_backend('ibm_...').properties()` (public FakeBackend snapshots suffice), a synthetic Rigetti-style crosstalk model, and an ion-trap T1-limited model with T1=10s, T2=1s. Re-run the n=4 d=2/3 sweep against each. Report per-device linear slopes and whether the depth-accumulation ratio remains close to gate-count ratio.

q: Can a noise-aware ansatz redesign (e.g., depth-adaptive VQE, hardware-native gate decomposition, symmetry-preserving ansatz for the TIsing Hamiltonian's Z2 symmetry) reduce the per-gate slope below the ~0.72-0.80 measured here?
basis: The paper adopts a generic hardware-efficient ansatz and does not attempt noise-aware ansatz design. Recent work (McClean et al. 2018, Grimsley et al. 2019 ADAPT-VQE, Bharti et al. 2022 review) argues that problem-adapted ansatze can achieve comparable expressivity with fewer gates, which would directly reduce the linear-slope coefficient. This is directly actionable and testable in our harness.
next_steps: Implement (a) a hardware-efficient ansatz restricted to the Z2-even subspace (parity-preserving CNOT + Rzz + Rx layers only, ~15 gates at n=4 d=2), and (b) an ADAPT-VQE built from a Pauli pool of {ZZ_ij, X_i} operators grown greedily until noiseless E/E_0 >= 0.98. Measure the linear DeltaE(p) slope for each; report slope-per-gate vs slope-per-VQE-precision-tradeoff. A slope reduction of >20% at fixed noiseless fidelity would validate noise-aware design as a lever.
